messages.subject: control lty-group assignment with legend
parts:
The example below appears to demonstrate that ggplot2 will *only* automatically create a legend if the group variable identified in aes() is a factor or a character.

But in that case the user exercises no direct control over which lty is assigned to which group.

Below, I work an example where I assign lty=1 to women and lty=2 to men, but obtain no legend; and in another example I obtain a legend but am unable to specify what lty is assigned to what group.

Is there an elegant and simple way to remedy this?

set.seed(1)
junk<-data.frame(x=-3:2)
junk<-rbind(
cbind(junk, gender="F")
,
cbind(junk, gender="M")
)
junk$y<-junk$x^2 / 3 + rnorm(nrow(junk)) / 6
junk$gender_lty<-c(M=2, F=1)[as.character(junk$gender)]
print(junk)
require(ggplot2)
# The following associates lty=2 with male and lty=1 with female,
# but it creates no legend to enlighten the reader.
print(
ggplot(data=junk, mapping=aes(x=x, y=y, group=gender_lty, lty=gender_lty) )
+ geom_line()
)
# This also creates no legend:
print(
ggplot(data=junk, mapping=aes(x=x, y=y, group=gender, lty=gender_lty) )
+ geom_line()
)
# The following does create a legend, but I have no control over the
# lty! Also, although factor() has associated the number 1 with women
# and 2 with men, ggplot2 gives lty=3 to men. So the numeric values of
# the factor have no bearing on which lty is given to which group.
print(
ggplot(data=junk, mapping=aes(x=x, y=y, group=gender, lty=gender) )
+ geom_line()
)
junk$whichNumberForWhichGender<-as.numeric(junk$gender)
print(junk)
# Finally, we observe the same behavior if the group variable is a
# character.
junk$chargender<-as.character(junk$gender)
print(str( junk$chargender))
print(
ggplot(data=junk, mapping=aes(x=x, y=y, group=chargender, lty=chargender) )
+ geom_line()
)

Thanks for any insight.

I really would like to decide which lty is assigned to which group, not allow a black box to make that decision it for me.

Jacob A. Wegelin

messages.subject: Re: control lty-group assignment with legend
parts:
Hi

The linetype cannot process continuous value.
Though it wokrs at this time,
in the future version, if you use continuous value for lty, it will be error.

You can manually control the linetype like this:

ggplot(junk, aes(x, y, lty=gender)) + geom_line() +
scale_linetype_manual(values=c(5, 6), breaks=c("F", "M"))

--

messages.author: 6d3f7222550fe21b
messages.subject: Re: control lty-group assignment with legend
parts: Thanks to all for their replies. Here is the example repeated with a simple and elegant solution thanks to Ista Zahn.

print(junk)
require(ggplot2)
# Suppose you are happy with the default linetypes and just want a
# different title or name for the legend:
print(
ggplot(data=junk, aes(x=x, y=y, group=gender, linetype=gender))
+ geom_line()
+ scale_linetype(
name="Gender"
)
)
# Suppose you want to personally exercise dominion over the linetype:
print(
ggplot(data=junk, aes(x=x, y=y, group=gender, linetype=gender))
+ geom_line()
+ scale_linetype_manual(
name="Gender"
, values=c(F=1, M=2)
)
)

Jacob Wegelin
